# ethereum-optimism/optimism Daily Update (Jun 18, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on enhancing `op-reth` with superchain-registry integration and payload builder improvements, alongside critical bug fixes in interop L2 contracts and SDM post-exec transaction handling. Documentation and testing efforts also saw significant updates.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### `op-reth` Enhancements and Superchain Integration
Significant progress was made in `op-reth`, with OP Mainnet and OP Sepolia chain specifications now loading from the embedded `superchain-registry`, eliminating hand-coded static configurations and reducing maintenance overhead ([#21397](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21397)). Additionally, the `op-reth` payload builder was updated to gate on the interop failsafe, preventing the sealing of interop transactions into unsafe blocks during failsafe windows ([#21448](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21448)).

### Critical Bug Fixes in Contracts and SDM
Several important bug fixes were implemented, addressing audit findings in interop L2 contracts, including stale NatSpec and incorrect blocked targets ([#21306](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21306)). The `op-rbuilder` was fixed to correctly append the trailing SDM PostExec transaction in the standard builder, ensuring compliance with OP consensus requirements ([#21332](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21332)). Furthermore, `alloy-op-evm` received a fix for over-refund bugs related to SDM warming rebates for never-cold accesses, along with hardened test suites ([#21434](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21434)).

### Documentation and Testing Improvements
Documentation for AI was updated to clarify that core OP Stack Rust crates were migrated, not vendored, into the monorepo ([#21469](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21469)). A new diagnostic pattern for CI-failure diagnosis on long-lived feature branches was added to the `ci-ops` documentation ([#21468](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21468)). Testing efforts included new SDM block-warming tests in `alloy-op-evm` to cover included-but-reverted transactions, ensuring correct behavior for cold EIP-2929 accesses ([#21466](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21466)).

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- **Infrastructure and Registry Updates:** New PRs include retrying package installs and network fetches in CI builds ([#21478](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21478)), integrating `l2cm` into `l2genesis` ([#21477](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21477)), caching submodules and pulling them outside the test step for `contracts-bedrock` CI ([#21476](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21476)), and coupling the superchain registry via a hoisted root submodule ([#21474](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21474)).
- **Documentation Updates:** Documentation updates include proxyd release notes to v4.29.0 ([#21473](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21473)) and adding the 2026-06 Interop L2 Contracts Cantina security review ([#21472](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21472)).

## CLOSED ISSUES

### Decoupling `op-geth` and Interop Contract Audits
The issue of creating `op-core/types` for OP-Stack-specific transaction and receipt types as part of the `op-geth` decoupling effort has been closed ([#20262](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20262)). This included the creation of `DepositTx` and `PostExecTx` types. Additionally, the re-audit of L2 interop contracts, including `CrossL2Inbox`, `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger`, `SuperchainETHBridge`, and `ETHLiquidity`, has been completed ([#20809](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20809)).

### ZK Proving and Local Development
Several issues related to ZK proving for CI and local development have been closed. This includes the issue of proposer integration with a self-hosted proving cluster, which was deemed unnecessary as `sp1-cluster` is already supported ([#21461](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21461)). The need for local/mock proving for CI and local debugging was also addressed ([#21418](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21418)), with the decision to use a mock prover for CI and local development ([#21409](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21409)). The definition of PROVE token management needs was also closed ([#21410](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21410)).

### L2 Calldata Compression Research
A research proposal for L2 Calldata Compression Proof was closed, with the feedback that closed-source algorithms are not useful for an L2 and that a fully open-source, audited implementation would be required for consideration ([#21471](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21471)).

## NEW ISSUES

### `op-node` and `op-reth` Syncmode Challenges
A new issue highlights that the default `syncmode.offset-el-safe` to 12h fails for `--minimal` nodes when running `op-node` v1.19.0 + `op-reth` v2.3.1 on various Superchain registry chains, leading to warnings about failing to insert unsafe payloads for EL sync ([#21465](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21465)).

### Superchain Registry State Management
A new issue identifies the need to couple `superchain-registry` state between `op-core`, `op-reth`, and `kona`, as currently, the registry commit/submodule needs to be changed in three individual places without checks to ensure they are in sync ([#21467](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21467)).

### `op-challenger` and Permissioned Games
An issue was opened regarding `op-challenger`, where permissioned games still require `cannon-prestate` in some cases, causing errors if the placeholder prestate cannot be found when `--prestate-url` is passed ([#21470](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21470)).

### Interop Security Narrative
A new issue proposes the creation of a security narrative for interop ([#21475](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21475)).

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### `kona-node` SafeDB and Syncmode Parity
Discussions around `kona-node`'s `SafeDB` ([#20278](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20278)) emphasize its interaction with interop and proofs, cautioning against blindly adopting `op-node`'s design. It's noted that `kona`'s EL node will persist the safe head after initial sync, potentially mitigating issues. The need for `syncmode.offset-el-safe` parity with `op-node` in `kona-node` ([#21243](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21243)) is also being addressed, with a recommendation to fix it soon and add a TODO to prioritize the safe DB when available, gathering requirements from Interop and Proofs for the new `SafeDB` design.

### SDM Operator Flag Consistency
The consistency of the SDM opt-in operator flag across `op-node`, `op-reth`, and `op-rbuilder` is being discussed ([#21360](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21360)). The scope will be narrowed to `op-reth` and `op-node`. There's a focus on standardizing the flag's name, with `operator_sdm_opt_in` being a strong candidate to clearly convey its purpose as a choice for chain operators to enable or disable SDM. The distinction between `protocol_active` (consensus/fork check) and the operator opt-in flag is also being clarified.
